target: Eu lia gibis o dia inteiro nas férias.
english: I used to read comics all day during vacation.
tip: 'Gibi' is the Brazilian word for comic book. It comes from a magazine that was extremely popular in the mid-20th century.

target: Enquanto a gente jantava, ele contou a novidade.
english: While we were having dinner, he shared the news.
tip: 'Enquanto' (while) + imperfect for background action; the main event uses preterite.

target: A gente passava as férias na casa dos avós.
english: We used to spend vacations at our grandparents' house.
tip: Imperfeito of -ar: passava (a gente). 'Passar as férias' = to spend vacation. 'Na casa dos avós' = at grandparents' house.

target: A casa era grande e tinha um quintal enorme.
english: The house was big and had a huge backyard.
tip: 'tinha' – diminutive suffix expressing smallness, affection, or informality, not just physical size.

target: Eu estudava nessa escola quando era criança.
english: I used to study at this school as a kid.
tip: Imperfeito of -ar: estudava (eu). 'Quando era criança' = when I was a child – also imperfeito.

target: A gente foi ao cinema ver um filme brasileiro.
english: We went to the movies to see a Brazilian film.
tip: 'Ir' past: a gente foi. 'Ir ao cinema' = to go to the movies. 'Ver' = to see/watch.

target: Eu não sabia que ele estava aqui até que o vi.
english: I didn't know he was here until I saw him.
tip: 'Sabia' (imperfeito, state of not knowing) + 'vi' (perfeito, moment of seeing). Discovery interrupted a state.

target: Eu comia muito doce quando era adolescente.
english: I used to eat a lot of candy as a teenager.
tip: Regular -er verbs in the imperfeito: -ia, -ia, -íamos, -iam. 'Comer' → 'comia.'

target: Eu ia à casa dele jogar videogame.
english: I used to go to his house to play video games.
tip: Reflexive pronoun placement follows strict rules: after the verb in affirmative imperatives, before it with negation.

target: Ela levava os filhos à escola de manhã.
english: She used to take the kids to school in the morning.
tip: Imperfeito of -ar: levava (ela). Habitual action: 'she used to take.' 'Levar à escola' = take to school.

target: Eu dormia tarde quando era estudante.
english: I used to go to bed late when I was a student.
tip: Regular -ir verbs in the imperfeito: -ia, -ia, -íamos, -iam. Same endings as -er verbs!

target: Ela se arrependeu de não ter ido.
english: She regretted not having gone.
tip: 'Arrepender-se de' means 'to regret.' This verb is always reflexive in Portuguese – there's no non-reflexive form.

target: A gente colecionava figurinhas.
english: We used to collect sticker cards.
tip: Collecting figurinhas (sticker albums, especially for the World Cup) is a beloved Brazilian tradition that spans generations.

target: Eu te falei sobre isso ontem.
english: I told you about this yesterday.
tip: 'Te' is the object pronoun for 'tu/você' (informal). In Brazil, 'te' is used with 'você' even though grammatically it belongs to 'tu.'

target: Eu te mostro as fotos depois.
english: I'll show you the photos later.
tip: Absolute superlatives add '-íssimo': 'rápido' → 'rapidíssimo' (extremely fast). This is common in speech for emphasis.

target: A gente brincava de esconde-esconde.
english: We used to play hide and seek.
tip: Imperfeito of -ar: brincava (a gente). 'Brincar de' + game = to play (a game). 'Esconde-esconde' = hide and seek.

target: Eu adorava as festas juninas.
english: I used to love the June festivals.
tip: Festas juninas are traditional June celebrations in Brazil with square dancing (quadrilha), corn-based foods, and bonfires. Huge cultural event.

target: Eu sonhava em morar no exterior.
english: I used to dream of living abroad.
tip: Imperfeito of -ar: sonhava (eu). 'Sonhar em' = to dream of. Describes an ongoing past aspiration.

target: Eu não te entendi, pode repetir?
english: I didn't understand you, can you repeat?
tip: 'Te' as direct object: 'não te entendi' = I didn't understand you. Pronoun before verb in negatives.

target: Ele me indicou um bom restaurante.
english: He suggested a good restaurant.
tip: 'Me' as indirect: 'me indicou' = recommended to me. 'Indicar' = to recommend/suggest.

target: Eles viajavam de carro para o litoral.
english: They used to drive to the coast.
tip: Imperfeito of -ar: viajavam (eles). Habitual action: 'they used to travel.' 'Litoral' = coast/beach area.

target: Todo mundo dançava quando a música parou.
english: Everyone was dancing when the music stopped.
tip: 'Dançava' (imperfeito, everyone was dancing) + 'parou' (perfeito, music stopped). Ongoing + sudden.

target: Ele me passou o telefone do médico.
english: He gave me the doctor's phone number.
tip: Some adjectives have Latin-derived superlatives: 'bom → ótimo', 'mau → péssimo', 'grande → máximo', 'pequeno → mínimo'.

target: Eu te achei mudado, está tudo bem?
english: I noticed you're different–is everything okay?
tip: The suffix '-íssimo/a' creates an absolute superlative: 'lindíssima' (extremely beautiful) – very expressive.

target: Nós jogávamos futebol na rua.
english: We used to play soccer in the street.
tip: Imperfeito of -ar: jogávamos (nós). 'Na rua' = in the street – common for childhood memories in Brazil.

target: A gente fazia churrasco todo domingo.
english: We used to have a barbecue every Sunday.
tip: Imperfeito of -er: fazia (a gente). 'Fazer' imperfeito: eu fazia, a gente fazia. Irregular stem.

target: A gente empinava pipa no morro.
english: We used to fly kites on the hill.
tip: 'Empinar pipa' (flying kites) is a beloved Brazilian childhood activity, especially in favelas and working-class neighborhoods.

target: Enquanto ele cozinhava, eu arrumei a mesa.
english: While he was cooking, I set the table.
tip: 'Enquanto' + imperfeito = while something was happening. The completed action uses perfeito.

target: A gente dançava forró toda sexta à noite.
english: We used to dance forró every Friday night.
tip: Imperfeito of -ar: dançava (a gente). 'Toda sexta à noite' = every Friday night. Habitual pattern.

target: Ele falava pouco quando era mais novo.
english: He used to talk little when he was younger.
tip: Imperfeito of -ar: falava (ele). 'Quando era mais novo' = when he was younger – imperfeito for age context.

target: Nós morávamos numa casa com jardim.
english: We used to live in a house with a garden.
tip: 'numa' contracts em+uma – mandatory in Portuguese, these preposition+article fusions are never written separately.

target: Ele trabalhava num banco antes de mudar de área.
english: He used to work at a bank before switching fields.
tip: Imperfeito of -ar: trabalhava (ele). 'Antes de' + infinitive = before doing something.

target: Eu me chamo Lucas.
english: My name is Lucas.
tip: 'Chamar-se' literally means 'to call oneself.' 'Me chamo Lucas' = I call myself Lucas. The most basic reflexive verb you'll learn.

target: Sem que ninguém perceba, ele saiu.
english: Without anyone noticing, he left.
tip: 'Sem que' always requires the subjunctive.

target: Eu me visto em cinco minutos.
english: I get dressed in five minutes.
tip: Reflexive verbs need a pronoun: `me chamo` (I'm called), `se levanta` (gets up). The pronoun matches the subject – me/te/se/nos/se.

target: Não existe professor que saiba tudo.
english: There's no teacher who knows everything.
tip: 'Seja' is the subjunctive of 'ser' – one of the most common subjunctive forms you'll encounter.

target: Não há ninguém que saiba disso.
english: There's no one who knows about this.
tip: Subjunctive is used after indefinite/negative antecedents.

target: Embora a comida esteja fria, está gostosa.
english: Although the food is cold, it's tasty.
tip: 'Embora' (although) always requires the subjunctive – it introduces a concession.

target: Não quero que ninguém saiba disso.
english: I don't want anyone to know about this.
tip: 'Querer que' always triggers the subjunctive – whenever one person wants another to do something.

target: Para mim, café é essencial de manhã.
english: For me, coffee is essential in the morning.
tip: 'Para mim' = for me (opinion/benefit). Don't confuse with 'por mim' = as far as I'm concerned / on my behalf.

target: Enquanto eu falava, ela anotava tudo.
english: While I was talking, she was writing everything down.
tip: Two simultaneous ongoing actions both use imperfeito: 'falava' and 'anotava' were happening at the same time.

target: Antes que a loja feche, preciso comprar pão.
english: Before the store closes, I need to buy bread.
tip: 'Antes que' always triggers the subjunctive – it signals uncertainty or a condition that may not be real.

target: A gente caminhava na praia quando viu o golfinho.
english: We were walking on the beach when we saw the dolphin.
tip: Past contrast: 'caminhava' (imperfeito, ongoing action) + 'viu' (perfeito, sudden event). 'Quando' often triggers this pattern.

target: Eu pensava que era fácil, mas descobri que não era.
english: I thought it was easy, but I found out it wasn't.
tip: 'Pensava' (imperfeito, ongoing belief) + 'descobri' (perfeito, completed discovery). Belief changed.

target: Obrigado por tudo.
english: Thank you for everything.
tip: 'Obrigado por' = thank you for. Use 'por' when thanking someone for something they already did. It's about the reason for your gratitude.

target: Ela lutou por seus direitos.
english: She fought for her rights.
tip: 'Por' for 'on behalf of' or 'in defense of': 'lutar por' = to fight for, 'votar por' = to vote for.

target: Vocês se lembram do aniversário dele?
english: Do you remember his birthday?
tip: 'Lembrar-se de' means 'to remember.' The 'se' makes it reflexive. You can also say 'lembrar de' without 'se' – both are correct in Brazil.

target: Para quando você precisa disso?
english: When do you need this?
tip: 'Para' for deadlines: 'para quando' = by when, 'para amanhã' = by tomorrow, 'para sexta' = by Friday.

target: Eu fiz isso para ajudar você.
english: I did this to help you.
tip: 'Para' expresses purpose – wHY you do something. 'Para ajudar' = in order to help. Think of 'para' as 'for the purpose of.'

target: A gente os recebeu de braços abertos.
english: We welcomed them with open arms.
tip: In informal Brazilian Portuguese, 'que' often replaces 'do que' in comparisons: 'maior que eu' instead of 'maior do que eu'.

target: Eu me esqueço de tudo o tempo todo.
english: I forget everything all the time.
tip: 'Esquecer-se de' is the reflexive form of 'to forget.' Both 'eu me esqueço' and 'eu esqueço' are used in Brazil with no difference in meaning.

target: A gente os deixou no hotel.
english: We dropped them off at the hotel.
tip: For equality, use 'tão...como' (as...as): 'Ela é tão inteligente como ele'. This pattern works with adjectives and adverbs.

target: Ela se maquiou rapidinho antes de sair.
english: She put on makeup quickly before leaving.
tip: 'Se maquiar' = to put on makeup. 'Rapidinho' = really quickly – diminutive of 'rápido' used as adverb.

target: Ela me deixou esperando meia hora.
english: She left me waiting for half an hour.
tip: 'Me' as direct: 'me deixou esperando' = left me waiting. 'Meia hora' = half an hour.

target: Nós nos divertimos muito no fim de semana.
english: We had a lot of fun on the weekend.
tip: 'Nos divertimos' – reciprocal/reflexive: we had fun. 'Nos' before verb. 'No fim de semana' = on the weekend.

target: Ele nos deu a melhor mesa do restaurante.
english: He gave us the best table at the restaurant.
tip: 'Melhor' (better/best) is the irregular comparative of 'bom' – never say 'mais bom'.

target: Ela me deixou sem palavras.
english: She left me speechless.
tip: 'Menos...do que' forms the comparative of inferiority – 'menos caro do que' (less expensive than).

target: Ele me tratou muito bem.
english: He treated me very well.
tip: 'Me' as direct: 'me tratou' = treated me. 'Muito bem' = very well.

target: Eu optei por ficar em casa.
english: I opted to stay home.
tip: 'Optar por' means 'to opt for/choose.' Some verbs always take 'por': optar por, lutar por, pagar por.

target: Ele me mandou embora mais cedo.
english: He sent me home early.
tip: The superlative uses definite article + 'mais' + adjective: 'o mais alto' (the tallest).
